paper_title: dKV-Cache The Cache for Diffusion Language Models
caption: Impact of batch size on decoding speed. Evaluated on LLaDA with a single NVIDIA H20; prefill length fixed at 100 tokens.
model_annotation: The line chart illustrates the relationship between batch size and decoding speed measured in tokens per second (Token/s) for different configurations of the dKV-Cache system and a baseline “Origin” model, evaluated on LLaDA using a single NVIDIA H20 GPU with a fixed prefill length of 100 tokens. The x-axis represents batch size, ranging linearly from 0 to 128, with tick marks at intervals of 20. The y-axis represents decoding speed in Token/s, ranging linearly from 0 to 225, with tick marks at intervals of 25. Six distinct lines are plotted: “L = 16” (gray solid line with square markers) starts at approximately 34.53 Token/s at batch size 0 and rises to 202.31 at batch size 128; “L = 32” (blue solid line with circle markers) begins at 38.45 and increases to 183.28; “L = 64” (red solid line with triangle markers) starts at 34.53 and reaches 130.58; “L = 128” (black solid line with diamond markers) begins at 34.53 and ends at 81.18; “dKV Cache-Decode” (black dashed line with triangle markers) starts at 34.53 and ends at 48.42; and “Origin” (gray dashed line with square markers) begins at 34.53 and ends at 69.62. All lines show a general upward trend with increasing batch size, though the rate of increase diminishes at higher batch sizes, and the “Origin” and “dKV Cache-Decode” lines remain relatively flat compared to the others.
